architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats and calculate the arithmetic mean of their SI_15_60 values. Accept the intervention as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if the mean SI_15_60 is below 3.80%. This is below half of the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% for reactive mass fraction 0.8000 and exceeds the declared 2.00 percentage-point discrimination resolution.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity transferred from another chemistry family; it is measured directly by the matched-window 120 C hold in S1C41. However, S1C41 is marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated, so the result supports only a formulation-level isothermal drift conclusion for this candidate and does not validate transfer of the unmodified-family temperature-response shape or broader chemistry-family generalization.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Using the arithmetic mean across at least two independent repeats, SI_15_60 at or above 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN and is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction. SI_15_60 below 3.80% falsifies H-CORE. A mean from 3.80% through below 7.61% falsifies neither hypothesis. Because both modifier axes are active, no outcome from this card separately falsifies H-RESIN versus H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a matched 120 C M-HOLD-120 acrylic-only control at 15.0% AC1920 with TK100 set to 0%, retaining the same reactive-core basis, 15/30/45/60 minute sampling, minimum two independent repeats, and prespecified mean-based thresholds. This isolates the minor-tackifier axis needed to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over the 15-60 minute window
judge_normalized.rationale: M-HOLD-120 is the most interpretable available measurement for viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C residence. S1C41 retains the supported E2 reactive-core basis while applying the smallest independently supported dual-axis modifier intervention among the tied top cards. The result can test whether drift is near the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction or substantially below 3.80%, while explicitly preserving the unresolved attribution between general resin suppression and minor-tackifier-dependent suppression. Conclusions remain formulation-level rheological conclusions only.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it is in the deterministic top set, uses the smallest dual-axis intervention in that tied set, and directly measures the declared failure mode. I followed the Skeptic on interpretation: the card separates low drift from the linear-dilution benchmark but cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL, and its modified chemistry does not support transfer of the unmodified thermal-response shape. The binding audit permits this direct-drift card while removing inadmissible modified-chemistry M-ANCHOR cards.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The dual-axis intervention is within the externally supported coarse modifier region, but local hold-stability evidence is sparse and the two modifier axes are not causally isolated.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Zero for the 120 C, 15-60 minute drift observable itself because the measurement directly samples the registered window; substantial for any temperature-shape transfer or generalization beyond S1C41.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The observable is directly calculated from measured viscosities at 15 and 60 minutes; the declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent repeats are required, with the arithmetic mean used for adjudication.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Moderate, because M-HOLD-120 does not control preparation or realization state; repeat-to-repeat process history and viscosity-scale variation may affect SI_15_60.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original reactive polyurethane hot-melt family centered on the E2 reactive core, including acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like modifier axes. The intended experiment should remain inside this family by retaining the audited reactive core and varying only registered modifier axes; applicability to any chemistry-changing modifier is not established until the upstream chemistry audit is loaded.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift)
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C matched-window measurements show SI_15_to_60 of 51.54% for E5 versus 9.51% for the least-drifting reference E1, with E5 reaching 93.08% by 90 min.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local temperature response is sampled from 80 to 130 C at six temperatures across multiple runs, although E2 shows large nominal spread with CV values of about 0.46-0.58. In contrast, the isothermal evidence covers only original E1 and E5, and the filtered state provides endpoint drift summaries rather than the underlying 15, 30, 45 and 60 min trajectories needed to distinguish linear dilution from superlinear suppression over the matched window.
measurement_requirements: Measure a matched 120 C isothermal hold at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min, with at least two independent repeats, and report SI_15_60 directly from the measured values.

Use the same reactive-mass basis and fully document acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like composition so the observed drift can be compared with the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction and the H-RESIN/H-DUAL alternatives.
Keep the analysis within the measured 15-60 min and 120 C window, without extrapolation or imputation.
planner.scientific_question: For a candidate in the original reactive polyurethane hot-melt chemistry family, is its matched-window 120 C viscosity drift consistent with linear dilution of the reactive core, or is it substantially below that prediction as required by resin-modification/superlinear-suppression behavior? The result must also record whether the acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes are active so that the tackifier-dependent H-DUAL explanation can be evaluated.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The primary observable is a direct matched-window 120 C thermal-hold drift measurement and does not depend on transferring the locally measured shared thermal-response shape into the modified chemistry. It is therefore measurement-admissible despite S1C41 being outside the validated unmodified chemistry family. The result must not be interpreted as evidence of validated thermal-shape transfer.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two independent repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and falsifies H-CORE at the declared 2.00% discrimination resolution. It establishes superlinear drift suppression relative to the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction, but does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both modifier axes are active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the observation is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction. A result below 3.80% would instead falsify H-CORE. The experiment cannot independently adjudicate H-RESIN versus H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift value from 3.80% through below 7.61% is intermediate: it decisively establishes neither the declared H-RESIN acceptance criterion nor the H-CORE falsification criterion. It would warrant a follow-up with an acrylic-only or otherwise axis-isolating composition to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is VOI-tied with S1C41, but uses a larger acrylic-like modifier burden without increasing hypothesis discrimination, uncertainty reduction, interpretability, or decision relevance.
It is VOI-tied with S1C41, but uses a larger acrylic-like modifier burden and therefore represents a less minimal intervention.
It is VOI-tied with S1C41, but uses a larger acrylic-like modifier burden and offers no additional separation of the registered hypotheses.
It is VOI-tied with S1C41, but uses the maximum acrylic-like loading in the tied set, making it the largest justified intervention without additional information value.

proposer.reasoning: The declared failure mode is directly measured by the matched 120 C hold, which is preferable to anchor or sweep measurements that do not resolve the isothermal-time coordinate. S1C41 lies within the externally supported 15-25% acrylic-like and approximately 5% minor-tackifier-like regions, has zero extrapolation risk in the VOI audit, and can distinguish the linear-dilution mechanism from low-drift behavior while remaining explicit about the unresolved H-RESIN versus H-DUAL pair.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and are genuinely tied. S1C41 is selected because it uses the lowest acrylic-like loading in the tied set, while retaining the independently supported 5% minor-tackifier-like level. This is the smallest sufficient total modifier burden within the directly supported intervention region and minimizes departure from the characterized local chemistry.

residual_decision_risk: H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain entangled because both modifier axes are active.
At least two repeats are required, but the rule for applying the 3.80% and 7.61% thresholds across repeats is unspecified.
The experiment has moderate process-state risk and does not control realization state.

S1C41 is in modified_chemistry_unvalidated resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 chemistry; direct SI_15_60 measurement is admissible, but unmodified shared thermal-shape transfer and broader chemistry-family generalization are unsupported.
The result supports formulation-level rheological conclusions only, not a molecular reaction or transport mechanism.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 together, and H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical predictions for this dual-axis composition. Thus a low-drift result can distinguish low drift from H-CORE but cannot identify whether suppression is attributable to resin modification generally or specifically to the minor-tackifier axis. The objection does not change which experiment should be run for the primary registered question of direct thermal-hold drift versus the linear-dilution benchmark; it changes the interpretation and requires an acrylic-only matched-window control as a follow-up if axis attribution is required. The repeat aggregation and threshold rule must also be prespecified.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the tied deterministic top set with four other S1C::M-HOLD-120 cards. The top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, the intervention-family and measurement-plan stabilities are both 1.0, and no recommendation_flip_boundary is reached for any weight term over the 0.5x-1.5x sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment is 0.004583. These weightings are defensible because M-HOLD-120 directly measures the declared thermal-hold failure mode in the registered 120 C, 15-60 minute window. This stability is decision stability of the transparent score, not confidence or evidence that the experiment is scientifically correct.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary SI_15_60 observable is directly measured by M-HOLD-120 at 120 C over the 15-60 minute window, so it does not reuse the unmodified shared thermal-response shape and is measurement-admissible. Nevertheless, S1C41 is explicitly marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated in resin_modified:ac1920+tk100. Direct measurement of this candidate is supported, but transfer of the unmodified 80-130 C thermal shape, or any broader chemistry-family generalization, would require a direct M-SWEEP verification in the modified chemistry.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: For S1C41, the protocol directly measures the relevant quantity and samples the exact registered 15-60 minute window. The H-CORE prediction is 7.608%, the H-RESIN/H-DUAL prediction is 3.804%, and the 3.804 percentage-point separation exceeds the declared 2.00% resolution. Thus results at or above 7.61% or below 3.80% are attainable decision regions. The repeat-level aggregation rule must still be prespecified.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support either superlinear resin behavior or tackifier-required behavior, so the experiment cannot identify which modifier axis accounts for suppression.
objections.objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict 3.804% drift at the selected 15% AC1920 plus 5% TK100 composition; their predicted difference is 0%, below the declared 2.00% discrimination resolution. The proposer correctly states this limitation in outcome_interpretation, but contradictorily lists all three hypotheses in hypotheses_separated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result can test dual-axis performance relative to linear dilution, but cannot support the H-DUAL attribution that TK100 is specifically required or establish that AC1920 alone is insufficient.
objections.objection: The formulation_state for S1C41 changes both registered modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0% and TK100 is 5.0%, with reactive_mass_fraction 0.8000. Because the primary hold compares only one dual-axis composition against the H-CORE prediction, any observed suppression cannot be attributed separately to the acrylic-like axis, the minor-tackifier-like axis, or their interaction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The drift measurement remains interpretable, but hypothesis adjudication could become ambiguous if one repeat crosses a threshold and the other does not.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 is directly measured from the specified 15, 30, 45 and 60 minute points under M-HOLD-120. It requires no fit, extrapolation, or imputation, so the proposer is correct that this is stronger evidence than M-ANCHOR or M-SWEEP for the stated failure mode. The remaining weakness is not the observable itself but the unspecified rule for aggregating the two repeats and handling their spread when applying the '<3.80%' or '>=7.61%' criteria.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct low-drift result could support a formulation-level observation for S1C41, but not validate the shared temperature-response shape or its applicability to resin-modified compositions.
objections.objection: The audit marks S1C41 as modified_chemistry_unvalidated in the resin_modified:ac1920+tk100 family, with shared_shape_use set to verification_only and no prior verified shape transfer. The direct M-HOLD-120 measurement is admissible because it observes the isothermal drift directly and does not reuse the unmodified shared thermal-response shape. Thus the primary SI_15_60 remains inside the measurement support of the protocol, but the experiment is outside the measured chemistry support for any claim about thermal-shape transfer or generalization from the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The thresholds are experimentally reachable, but borderline or discordant repeat results may not yield a reproducible falsification decision.
objections.objection: The stated thresholds are numerically attainable by M-HOLD-120: for S1C41, H-CORE predicts 7.608%, H-RESIN/H-DUAL predict 3.804%, and the declared 2.00% resolution is smaller than the 3.804 percentage-point separation from H-CORE. A result at or above 7.61% can therefore falsify H-RESIN, and a result below 3.80% can falsify H-CORE under the registered rules. However, the protocol specifies only 'at least two independent repeats' and does not define whether the criterion applies to every repeat, the mean, or a confidence/uncertainty bound.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be misreported as identifying a molecular reaction or transport mechanism when it only discriminates phenomenological drift behavior at one composition and one hold window.
objections.objection: The direct hold can establish whether the observed matched-window drift is below or near the registered linear-dilution benchmark, but it cannot establish the molecular explanation stated in H-RESIN, such as reduced encounter frequency or an effective non-reactive continuum. The payload's claim boundary explicitly limits the hypotheses to formulation-level rheological mechanisms, so language implying molecular mechanism would exceed what M-HOLD-120 measures.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a matched acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 control at the same AC1920 loading and reactive-core basis with TK100 set to zero, using the same 120 C, 15-30-45-60 minute protocol and repeat rule. This is the necessary axis-isolating comparison for distinguishing H-RESIN from H-DUAL; also prespecify whether threshold decisions use each repeat, the repeat mean, or an uncertainty interval.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 changes AC1920 and TK100 together, while H-RESIN and H-DUAL make identical 3.804% predictions for that dual-axis composition. Therefore the experiment can distinguish low drift from the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction, but cannot determine whether suppression is due to resin modification generally or specifically to the minor-tackifier axis.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is BINDING. The cards it marks inadmissible were removed before ranking and are not selectable. You may state that you disagree with the rule and why; naming a removed card is an invalid output.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
